# COR100 `misleading-inline-if-semicolon`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

A statement follows a one-line `if` after a semicolon: it is not conditional.

## Why

In `if (c) a = 1; b = 2` only `a = 1` depends on the condition: the semicolon ends the `if`
statement, and `b = 2` always executes, although the line reads as if both were guarded. Use an
`if ... then ... end if` block or put the second statement on its own line.

## Reported

```fortran
if (err /= 0) print *, 'failed'; stop
```

## Preferred

```fortran
if (err /= 0) then
  print *, 'failed'
  stop
end if
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[COR100] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = COR100` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `C151` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
